definitions.explanation: A small motorized vehicle with an engine displacement of 50cc or less. Abbreviated from {原動機付自転車|げんどうきつきじてんしゃ}. Requires only a basic license and can be ridden from age 16 in Japan.

examples.japanese: {原付|げんつき}で{通学|つうがく}している。
examples.english: I commute to school by moped.

examples.japanese: {原付|げんつき}の{制限速度|せいげんそくど}は{時速|じそく}30キロだ。
examples.english: The speed limit for mopeds is 30 km/h.

examples.japanese: {高校生|こうこうせい}の{時|とき}に{原付|げんつき}の{免許|めんきょ}を{取|と}って、{毎日|まいにち}バイト{先|さき}まで{乗|の}っていた。
examples.english: I got my moped license in high school and rode it to my part-time job every day.

notes:
An abbreviation of {原動機付自転車|げんどうきつきじてんしゃ} (engine-equipped bicycle). In everyday speech, {原付|げんつき} is far more common than the full form. These small scooters are extremely popular in Japan for short-distance commuting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原付|げんつき}{免許|めんきょ}: moped license
- {原付|げんつき}に{乗|の}る: to ride a moped
- {原付|げんつき}の{制限速度|せいげんそくど}: moped speed limit
- {原付|げんつき}{二種|にしゅ}: Class 2 moped (51-125cc)

REGULATIONS:
- Maximum speed: 30 km/h
- Two-stage right turns required at large intersections
- No passengers allowed
- License obtainable at age 16 with a written test only

SIMILAR WORDS:
- バイク: motorcycle — general term for any motorbike
- スクーター: scooter — often refers to the same vehicles but emphasizes the step-through design
- {自動二輪|じどうにりん}: motorcycle (over 50cc) — the legal category above {原付|げんつき}
